item.text: {"chapter_reviews":[{"attribution_risk":"medium","bias_review":{"allegations_vs_findings":"Generally separated: official enforcement totals are treated as activity rather than proof of deterrence; PAPI/PCI report experiences and perceptions; and the State Audit records formal findings rather than allegations. Residual risk remains where state reporting frames scandals, discipline, and removals without independent case-level or due-process verification.","closed_system_silence":"High residual risk. The notebook identifies censorship, restricted information, limited procurement transparency, and no independent auditing mechanism; official silence cannot establish absence of misconduct, selectivity, or implementation failure.","duplicate_reporting":"Material duplication is controlled imperfectly. WD004 is a landing-page version of the World Bank assessment subsequently captured more precisely in WEB-8B-C1-006 and should not be counted separately. WD010’s imprecise GDP locator is superseded for precise extraction by WEB-8B-C2-011, which is context rather than final evidence. Official government, Vietnam News Agency, Viet Nam News, NSO, Vietnam Social Security, and State Audit material is substantially one state-information family, even where it documents different facts.","favorable_and_adverse_search":"Both were performed. Favorable formal-program, enforcement, recovery, and diplomatic evidence is paired with World Bank implementation evidence, PAPI and PCI surveys, BTI assessments, audit findings, and adverse foreign-policy analyses.","missing_source_type":"The principal unresolved bias risk is ruler-specific attribution for personnel choice and corrective action. Missing are independently accessible deliberative/personnel records or credible contemporaneous insider/institutional scholarship identifying Trọng’s comparative selection role, plus independent causal evaluation of whether a ruler-linked correction changed implementation before year-end.","official_claim_independence":"Partly checked. IMF and World Bank corroborate macro/program context, while PAPI, PCI, BTI, ISEAS, East Asia Forum, and The Diplomat provide independent perspectives. Formal directives, committee formation, enforcement totals, personnel procedures, fiscal-close figures, and audit findings still rely predominantly on official institutional reporting; the audit is authoritative but not independent of the Vietnamese state.","open_system_complaint_volume":"PAPI and PCI add necessary adverse outcome evidence, but their reported perceptions and firm experiences are not direct prevalence or causal measures. Complaint/perception volume can reflect salience, reporting conditions, respondent mix, or enforcement visibility and should not be read as a simple severity count.","population_exposure_authority_baseline_shocks":"Substantially addressed: the notebook identifies shared authority, collective procedures, ministerial and provincial implementation, reopening and the low 2021 base, external demand, Chinese disruptions, Ukraine-related shocks, and inherited coordination weaknesses. It does not fully quantify differential population exposure or isolate the marginal effect of each authority holder or shock.","supporting_evidence_ids":["WD001","WD002","WD003","WD005","WD006","WD007","WD008","WD009","WD011","WD012","WEB-8B-C1-003","WEB-8B-C1-006","WEB-8B-C1-007","WEB-8B-C1-009","WEB-8B-C1-010","WEB-8B-C2-001","WEB-8B-C2-003","WEB-8B-C2-004","WEB-8B-C2-005","WEB-8B-C2-008","WEB-8B-C2-009","WEB-8B-C2-010"],"unresolved_risks":["No evidence establishes Trọng’s personal comparative evaluation or choice of replacement implementers; collective authority limits, but does not eliminate, responsibility-based attribution.","No source causally links a specific Trọng directive or government correction to improved implementation before the end of 2022.","Closed information conditions and state-family concentration limit inference about enforcement selectivity, underlying corruption, due process, and unreported administrative failure.","Later audit evidence supports durability analysis but cannot be treated as a target-period event or as information available by year-end 2022.","Survey evidence measures experience and perception, not a complete national incidence measure or personal causal responsibility."]},"chapter_id":"8B","defensible_evidence_estimate":29,"independent_source_family_estimate":10,"missing_themes":["8B.4: ruler-specific evidence of Trọng’s role, criteria, and comparative judgment in selecting or empowering 2022 replacement implementers, distinct from collective procedure.","8B.8: target-period evidence that a ruler-linked corrective action, rather than a government-wide response, measurably improved implementation or administrative initiative before year-end.","8B.5–8B.7 and 8B.10: independently verifiable evidence on enforcement quality, selectivity, due process, deterrence, recurrence, and underlying corruption beyond official activity counts and survey perceptions.","8B.10: durable program-performance evidence that can separate recovery-program execution from reopening, export demand, inherited capacity, and shared governmental responsibility."],"substantive_issues":["WD004 is a gateway/landing-page presentation and duplicates the underlying World Bank report captured in WEB-8B-C1-006; it is excluded from the defensible estimate.","WD010 has an imprecise locator and is superseded for exact extraction by context record WEB-8B-C2-011; neither is needed to establish the broader independently qualified recovery analysis.","Official source-family concentration is substantial for formal enforcement, personnel, fiscal-execution, and audit claims; multiple outlets do not constitute independent corroboration.","The dossier appropriately states attribution limits, but some formal state actions remain only authority-based rather than evidence of personal direction or operational ownership."]}],"global_findings":["Terminal conclusion: research rounds were exhausted without full saturation; this is not a claim that the dossier is complete.","The selected 8B scope has materially varied evidence, including direct program and directive evidence, independent economic and survey-based contrary evidence, and multiple foreign-policy analyses.","No further continuation is requested under the immutable terminal instruction. Residual source-quality, attribution, and closed-system risks must carry forward to downstream confidence and interpretation.","Defensible evidence excludes discovery-only/context items and duplicated or gateway-only copies; count estimates are source-claim units, not independent confirmations."],"needs_continuation":false,"reviewer_summary":"The 8B dossier is adequate for a qualified, balanced evidence handoff across the selected lenses, but not saturated. It supports formal program, institutional mobilization, mixed implementation, and constrained diplomatic-management claims while preserving material limits on personal attribution, durable effectiveness, and visibility in a closed information environment.","schema_version":"ruler_evidence_review_v1","selected_theme_ids":[]}
